_meta.role: Embedded Software Engineer II, Ring Firmware

summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY with embedded firmware experience in C/C++ on ARM Cortex-M4 (STM32): bare-metal peripheral drivers, interrupt service routines, and FreeRTOS tasking over UART/I2C/SPI. Built a low-level I2C driver and timer-triggered ADC firmware in 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM, and integrated Bluetooth, ToF sensors, and Jetson-to-microcontroller links across hardware and software boundaries.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove for hands-free cursor control integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth wireless link, translating 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed a Python GUI using PyQt and Matplotlib for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization in a laboratory environment.
Used GitLab for version control and JupyterHub for collaborative data analysis and technical documentation.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C on ARM Cortex-M4 (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at deterministic 1 Hz update rate; verified in Proteus.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt service routine (ISR) sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver.
Built Cortex-M4 temperature monitoring firmware in embedded C with timer-synchronized sensing and real-time display.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination on STM32; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands and user override.

projects.name: Robocon Competition Robot — Holonomic Drive & Encoder Odometry
bullets: Implemented interrupt-driven quadrature decoding from first principles — a 4-bit A/B transition state machine on hardware interrupts — and drove four motor channels at 15 kHz PWM via DuePWM.

Integrated Xbox 360 control over USB Host Shield with 4x Cytron motor drivers, dual claw subsystems with per-claw IR sensing, and a catapult thrower; added a fail-safe state machine halting all motors on controller disconnect.
projects.note: SELECTION GUIDANCE, not resume text. Undergraduate robotics-club work at FCRIT, not professional experience. Include when the JD asks for motor control, encoders, odometry or closed-loop feedback — this is the only evidence for those. Otherwise prefer 'STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor' and the COFFIN capstone, which are stronger work. Never place it first, and never let it crowd out COFFIN on an edge-AI role.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Integrated faster-whisper STT (1.0–1.4s), Gemini intent classification (<500ms), TensorRT-optimized YOLO (5.2× speedup: 56.7→10.9 ms, 17.6→92 FPS vs eager PyTorch) for visual servoing, and dual VL53L0X ToF sensors (camera range-gate + gripper-ToF-triggered close at 25 mm) for contact-aware grasping via TCA9548A I2C mux.
Resolved 11 integration failures (false-positive detections, servo brown-out, stale-frame capture); achieved 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s end-to-end voice-to-picked latency.
